sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: International Student Placement and Golden Visa Residence Advisory

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Taiwan, China (cross-strait investor source; entity-formation jurisdiction is mainland China)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA) between the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) and the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF), effective 29 June 2010
Cross-Strait Investment Protection and Promotion Agreement (CSIPPA), effective 1 February 2013

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (revised 25 April 2024, effective 1 January 2025); Administrative Measures for the Beneficial Owner Information of Market Entities (PBOC and SAMR Order No. 3 [2024], effective 1 November 2024); Foreign Investment Law of the PRC (2020) and its Implementing Regulations; Taiwan-region Money Laundering Control Act, as amended through 2018; Taiwan-region Company Act, Article 22-1, requiring registration of substantial controllers with the Ministry of Economic Affairs; and the applicable AML/CFT examination regulations for non-financial businesses.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Business License) of the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Taiwan destination: PRC notary office notarization followed by ARATS cross-strait verification and SEF certification; Hague Apostille is not available because the Taiwan region is not an Apostille Convention party. For Hague Convention destinations: PRC notary office notarization followed solely by apostille from the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs; consular legalization must never be added after an apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Continued Registration / No Serious Illegal Record)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Provincial or municipal SAMR branch of the registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel authentication paths are mutually exclusive: (1) for Taiwan, PRC notarization plus ARATS/SEF cross-strait verification; (2) for Hague member states, PRC notarization plus apostille by the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs; never combine apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing incorporation, name clearance, and bank account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors / incorporators / proposed legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original signatures and corporate seals must be notarized by a licensed PRC notary. For Taiwan, the notarized document must be verified through ARATS and certified by SEF. For Hague states, the notarized document must be apostilled by the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The two authentication paths are exclusive and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (and Joint Venture Contract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The governing Chinese text must be notarized by a PRC notary office. For Taiwan use, cross-strait verification through ARATS and SEF is required; for Hague member states use apostille only. Consular legalization is not superimposed on apostille for any instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Taiwan-region investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank maintaining the investor's operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If addressed to PRC authorities, the bank officer's signature and bank seal must be notarized in Taiwan and then submitted through SEF/ARATS verification for use in mainland China; this is the consular-legalization-equivalent cross-strait path. If the document is to be used in a Hague Convention state, Taiwan-region authorities cannot issue a valid Hague apostille; instead, use Taiwan-region notarization followed by authentication by the Taiwan-region Ministry of Foreign Affairs and consular legalization by the destination country's representative office where required. Do not treat Taiwan-region authentication as a Hague apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Declaration / Beneficial Owner Information Report
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Legal representative and each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified signatures must be notarized by a PRC notary, then either verified through ARATS/SEF for Taiwan-related filing or apostilled by the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Hague jurisdictions. The report itself is filed only in the PBOC/SAMR government-access beneficial owner database; it is not a public record.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before accepting the engagement and before any equity subscription, the compliance partner must screen all proposed UBOs, directors, shareholders, and authorized signatories against OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) and Non-SDN Consolidated Screening

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (Act No. 1 of 1929, as amended), particularly Articles 1-10, 128-156 (incorporation), 192-206 (directors), and the Investment Approval Regulations under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce, Company Registration
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (公司章程) and Application for Company Registration
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for general companies in Taiwan; however, for a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture, the Investment Commission of MOEA requires a capital adequacy assessment. The capital must be fully subscribed and paid-in within the period specified in the investment approval. No escrow account is mandated, but funds must be remitted from abroad and deposited in a local bank account, with a capital verification report issued by a certified public accountant.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the Board of Directors of [Company Name] (the "Company") hereby adopts the following resolutions at its first meeting held on [Date] at [Place]:

1. Share Capital Subscription: The Board acknowledges the subscription of the Company's share capital as set forth in the Articles of Incorporation. The total authorized share capital is [Amount] New Taiwan Dollars (NTD), divided into [Number] shares of [Par Value] each. The initial paid-in capital is [Amount] NTD, which has been fully subscribed by the shareholders in accordance with the Investment Approval granted by the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs. The Board confirms that all contributions have been received and directs the Chief Financial Officer to deposit the funds into the Company's designated bank account and to complete all statutory capital filings within the prescribed period.

2. Banking Authorization: The Board hereby authorizes the opening of a corporate bank account with [Bank Name] and designates the following individuals as authorized signatories: [Name], [Title], and [Name], [Title]. Any two of the authorized signatories shall jointly sign all checks, drafts, and other banking instruments on behalf of the Company. The Board further authorizes the use of online banking systems subject to the same dual-signature requirement. The bank is instructed to honor all instructions from the Company in accordance with this mandate.

3. Registered Office Adoption: The Board adopts the registered office of the Company at [Address], Taiwan, as the official legal place for service of process and all statutory correspondence. The Company Secretary is directed to file the registered office address with the Department of Commerce and to ensure that all official notices are received and processed promptly.

4. Statutory Officer Appointments: The Board appoints the following officers: [Name] as Chairperson of the Board, [Name] as Managing Director, [Name] as Company Secretary, and [Name] as Chief Financial Officer. Each officer shall have the powers and duties as prescribed by the Taiwan Company Act and the Articles of Incorporation. The Board authorizes the Company Secretary to execute all necessary documents and to represent the Company in all statutory filings and registrations.

5. General Ratification: The Board resolves that all actions taken by the shareholders, promoters, and officers in connection with the incorporation and registration of the Company are hereby ratified and confirmed. The Board further resolves that this resolution shall be effective immediately and shall be recorded in the minutes of this meeting.

This resolution is passed unanimously by the Board of Directors on the date first written above.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Investment Approval from MOEA Investment Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formal application for foreign investment approval via the MOEA Investment Commission online portal. The application must include a detailed business plan, capital structure, shareholder identification, and a feasibility study. Provide notarized copies of the foreign investor's certificate of incorporation, audited financial statements, and a power of attorney authorizing the local representative. The Commission will review the application for compliance with the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals and may request additional information. The approval is a prerequisite for company registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized certificate of incorporation of foreign investor
Audited financial statements of foreign investor (last 2 years)
Passport copies of shareholders and directors
Power of attorney for local representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond with supplementary documentation within 14 days. If rejected, file an appeal with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days of the rejection notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan Notary Public and Department of Commerce (pre-approval)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Taiwan attorney to draft the Articles of Incorporation in Chinese, incorporating all mandatory clauses under the Company Act, including share capital, shareholder rights, director powers, and registered office. The Articles must be executed by all shareholders and notarized by a Taiwan notary public. After notarization, submit the Articles to the Department of Commerce for pre-approval if required. Ensure that all signatures are properly notarized and that the document complies with the Investment Approval conditions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or Department of Commerce requests amendments, revise the Articles and resubmit within 10 days. If pre-approval is denied, address the specific objections and reapply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Company Registration to Department of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the completed company registration application with the Department of Commerce, attaching the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the Investment Approval, and the capital verification report. The application must list the registered office, directors, supervisors, and the company's business scope. The Department will review the submission and, upon satisfaction, issue the Company Registration Certificate. This certificate is the legal proof of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Capital verification report from a certified public accountant
Consent forms from directors and supervisors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended or rejected, provide the missing documents or correct the errors within 7 days. If the rejection is upheld, appeal to the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Tax Identification and Obtain Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Administration (Ministry of Finance) and local municipal government
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Company Registration Certificate, apply for a Tax Identification Number (TIN) with the National Taxation Administration. Simultaneously, apply for a business registration certificate from the local municipal government. For the specific business scope of study abroad and immigration visa consulting, obtain the required industry licenses: an Immigration Consultant License from the National Immigration Agency (NIA) and a Study Abroad Agency Registration from the Ministry of Education. Submit all required documents, including the company registration certificate, director identification, and proof of professional qualifications.
required_dossiers: Immigration Consultant License application (including professional qualifications)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax registration is delayed, follow up with the taxation office. If the industry license is denied, submit an appeal to the respective ministry within 30 days, providing additional evidence of compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Corporate Bank Account and Deposit Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Company Registration Certificate, the board resolution authorizing the bank account, and the identification of authorized signatories to the chosen bank. Open a corporate account and deposit the paid-in capital. Obtain a capital verification report from a certified public accountant, which is required for final registration and for the issuance of the Company Registration Certificate. Ensure that the bank account is fully operational and that all signatories are registered with the bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional documentation, provide the requested items within 5 days. If the bank rejects the application, select an alternative bank and repeat the process.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: National Immigration Agency (NIA), Ministry of the Interior; and Ministry of Education (for study abroad placement)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Immigration Consultant License (移民業務機構許可) and Study Abroad Agency Registration (留學服務業登記)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no physical manufacturing or warehousing; however, the office must comply with general workplace safety regulations under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including fire safety equipment and emergency exits, as verified by the local fire department.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Taxation Administration (Taiwan), acting through the National Taxation Bureau and local tax offices; online electronic portal: the Ministry of Finance Tax Registry and e-Filing Platform (mof.gov.tw) and the e-Invoice Cloud Service (einvoice.nat.gov.tw)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity forming a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture in Taiwan must first obtain investment approval from the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs, then apply for business registration with the National Taxation Bureau to receive a statutory Unified Business Number/Tax Identification Number (TIN). The application requires the approved Articles of Incorporation, foreign company certification, domestic address or leased premise proof, responsible-person identity documents, and the investment approval letter. After the TIN is issued, the JV must complete VAT business registration under the Business Tax Act before commencing taxable sales. If the foreign entity has no fixed place of business in Taiwan, the TIN and VAT registration application must be filed through a qualified withholding agent or duly appointed domestic tax representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for corporate entity classification; Taiwan does not offer check-the-box pass-through elections for a limited company. The only relevant administrative election is application for small-scale enterprise treatment under the Business Tax Act when average monthly sales revenue is below NT$200,000, which subjects qualified enterprises to a 1% business tax rate instead of standard VAT, but the entity remains an entity-level taxpayer for income tax; hybrid mismatch elections are not separately available in Taiwan.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Business Tax under the Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax Act)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no general VAT registration exemption; all enterprises selling goods or services in Taiwan are required to register. However, businesses with average monthly revenue below NT$200,000 may qualify for simplified lump-sum business-tax treatment at 1% for value-added enterprises or 4% for non-value-added enterprises; once average monthly turnover reaches or exceeds NT$200,000, the enterprise is subject to mandatory full VAT registration, issuance of uniform invoices, and normal VAT compliance.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan mandates the Uniform Invoice System, including electronic Uniform Invoices (e-Invoices) under the Ministry of Finance integration service. Registered VAT taxpayers, particularly B2B and high-volume B2C businesses, must integrate with the e-Invoice platform through certified turnkey software or API using tax-entity digital certificates; e-invoice data, invoice numbers, and carrier information must be uploaded to the Ministry of Finance platform for recording. Real-time clearance is not imposed for every invoice, but Taiwan enforces platform-based digital stamping through the unique Uniform Invoice number, seller identifier, encryption mechanism, and anti-fraud controls such as the GUI authentication code and carrier validation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Business Tax Act, zero-rated export treatment applies to: (1) goods exported from Taiwan under customs control; (2) services directly related to exported goods or international transport; and (3) services rendered by a Taiwanese enterprise for an offshore party where the entire service is used or supplied outside Taiwan and the consideration is received in foreign currency. For the study-abroad and immigration visa consultancy services of the JV, offshore client services must be contractually supplied to non-residents, performed for destinations outside Taiwan, and invoiced and collected in foreign currency to qualify for the 0% VAT rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) issued by Taiwan Customs
Bill of Lading or air waybill evidencing physical export of any goods
Commercial invoice and export packing list
Foreign exchange inward remittance certificate or Foreign Exchange Settlement Water issued by a designated bank showing receipt of the foreign currency proceeds
Bilingual or English-language service contract or agreement identigying the offshore customer, service scope, and payment terms
Uniform Invoice or e-Invoice in the export series issued to the foreign buyer where required
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Taiwan tax authorities may deny zero-rating, reassess the uncollected 5% VAT, impose penalty surcharges and interest, and issue fines of up to five times the amount of tax due when mandatory export documentation is missing, false, or inconsistent. Where foreign-exchange repatriation does not occur within 180 days from the export or service supply date and no valid exception exists, the zero-rating claim is presumed unsubstantiated and subject to retrospective clawback, additional penalties, and enhanced audit scrutiny, including potential anti-money-laundering reporting under Taiwan financial regulations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Company Filing and Financial Statement Submission (公司年度申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Affairs, Corporate E-Filing Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 1 March and 30 June for the fiscal year ending 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs an administrative fine of NT$10,000 (approximately USD 320) plus an order to rectify; repeated non-compliance escalates to NT$50,000 (approximately USD 1,600) and persistent failure may trigger administrative dissolution by the MOEA.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Return (營利事業所得稅結算申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (local issue office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 May through 31 May immediately following the calendar tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing/payment triggers a delinquency surcharge of 1% every two days, capped at 15%, plus monthly interest; willful underreporting attracts a penalty of up to three times the underpaid tax and potential criminal prosecution of responsible officers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Operation Performance Report (外資投資事業營運狀況申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 April for the preceding calendar year via the MOEAIC online reporting portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or false declaration results in fines under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals of up to NT$50,000 (approximately USD 1,600); repeat violations may suspend future investment approvals, profit remittances, and permit renewals for the JV.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Shareholders, Adoption of Financial Statements, and Filing of Resolutions (if required)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company records maintained at the registered office; resolutions filed with MOEA where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after each fiscal year-end (by 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to convene the AGM within the statutory window may be fined NT$10,000 to NT$100,000 (approximately USD 320 to 3,200) under the Company Act; the MOEA may order an extraordinary general meeting and impose escalating fines for continued default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO Annual Confirmation and Shareholding Register Maintenance (公司主要股東及最終受益人申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Central Company Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the company filing by 30 June; any share transfer or control change must be reported within 15 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission or misstatement of beneficial ownership data exposes the company and responsible officers to fines of NT$50,000 to NT$500,000 (approximately USD 1,600 to 16,000), with repeated violations triggering liability for each individual default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business and Tax Registration Certificate Renewal and Change Maintenance (營利事業登記)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Department of Finance / District National Taxation Bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based renewal; immediate filing of any change in registered address, shareholders, directors, or business scope
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to renew or update registration attracts fines of NT$10,000 to NT$100,000 (approximately USD 320 to 3,200); prolonged non-compliance may lead to suspension of the tax registration and revocation of the taxable business license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Immigration Agency (Study Abroad and Visa Services) Annual License and Operational Statement (移民業務機構年度申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Immigration Agency, Ministry of the Interior; municipal education authorities for study-abroad counseling where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual renewal and operational statement within 30 days after the license anniversary; for new JV licenses, before each calendar year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating under an expired or unrenewed license constitutes unlicensed immigration consultancy: fines up to NT$200,000 (approximately USD 6,400), immediate cease-and-desist orders, and criminal liability for responsible persons under the Immigration Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audited financial statements by a Taiwan-licensed CPA are required when the JV's paid-in capital exceeds NT$30 million (approximately USD 960,000), for banks, insurance, financial holding companies, and publicly traded enterprises, or when the MOEA imposes CPA certification upon application for shareholder transfer, capital increase, or profit distribution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan GAAP under the Commercial Accounting Act and the Regulations on Business Entity Accounting Handling; enterprises may elect IFRS or the simplified Taiwan Enterprise Accounting Standard aligned with IFRS for SMEs; non-corporate taxpayers follow the same framework for tax-basis bookkeeping.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The JV must renew its UBO declaration annually through the MOEA company registry e-filing system, stating all natural persons who directly or indirectly hold more than 25% of shares or exercise controlling influence; any share transfer or change in control must be registered and verified with updated notarized or apostilled corporate documents within 15 days; the MOEA may cross-check against tax and AML financial intelligence records, and annual audited shareholder lists must reconcile with the register of members.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / Shareholders (股東名簿) with full ownership history and pledged/escrowed shares
Register of Directors and statutory officers (董事及經理人名單)
Minute Book of Shareholders' General Meetings and Directors' Meetings (股東會及董事會議事錄)
UBO and Principal Shareholder Beneficial Ownership Register (公司主要股東及最終受益人申報)
Annual Financial Statements, Audit Reports, and tax bookkeeping schedules

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 to USD 1,200 per year for a Taiwan registered office address and statutory corporate agent service, including legal process reception and correspondence forwarding
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 to USD 6,000 per year for a certified CPA audit of a medium-sized consulting joint venture under Taiwan GAAP, including compilation of tax-basis adjustment schedules
